paragraphs.paragraph: Kindness and Protection in Times of Trouble
paragraphs.title: Kindness and Protection in Times of Trouble

answers: The person who considers the poor
The enemies of the righteous
Only a wealthy person
easy.explanation: The verse blesses the person who thoughtfully considers the poor.
easy.q: Whom does the opening verse bless?

answers: Give him great riches
Deliver him
Send him to another country
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.”
easy.q: What will the LORD do for the person who considers the poor in time of trouble?

answers: In the battlefield
On a journey
Upon the bed of languishing
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing.
easy.q: Where will the LORD strengthen the suffering person?

answers: Showing kindness to the poor is followed by God’s preservation and help
Helping the poor causes enemies to triumph
Helping the poor is described as meaningless
medium.explanation: The passage connects consideration for the poor with God’s deliverance, preservation, and support.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between considering the poor and God’s care?

answers: Turns away from
Thinks carefully about and shows concern for
Punishes
medium.explanation: In this context, “considereth” means thoughtfully understanding and caring about the poor.
medium.q: What does “considereth” mean in “he that considereth the poor”?

answers: Sickness, exile, and defeat
Riches, victory, and kingship
Deliverance, preservation, and support in sickness
medium.explanation: The passage speaks of deliverance in trouble, preservation and life, and strength during sickness.
medium.q: Which sequence best summarizes the promises in these verses?

answers: God’s care reaches both general trouble and physical illness
The passage is only about poverty
Illness is presented only as punishment for enemies
challenge.explanation: The passage expands the idea of God’s care from trouble generally to sickness and weakness.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “time of trouble” to “the bed of languishing” suggest?

answers: That the sick person needs no help
That God’s care extends throughout the person’s sickness
That the person moves from place to place
challenge.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes the completeness of God’s care during illness.
challenge.q: What does “all” emphasize in “thou wilt make all his bed in his sickness”?

answers: Both seek harm for others
Both hide their actions
Both respond to suffering with care and help
challenge.explanation: The person considers the poor, while the LORD preserves and strengthens the suffering person.
challenge.q: What quality is shared by the person described at the beginning and the LORD described afterward?

paragraphs.idea: Kindness and Protection in Times of Trouble

paragraphs.paragraph: A Plea for Healing Amid Hostile Enemies
paragraphs.title: A Plea for Healing Amid Hostile Enemies

answers: Mercy and healing
Victory in battle
Wealth and honor
easy.explanation: He says, “LORD, be merciful unto me: heal my soul.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask of the LORD?

answers: That he would rule over them
That he would die and his name perish
That he would help them
easy.explanation: They ask, “When shall he die, and his name perish?”
easy.q: What do the psalmist’s enemies want to happen to him?

answers: His familiar friend, in whom he trusted
One of the poor
All his enemies together
easy.explanation: The passage describes a trusted familiar friend who ate the psalmist’s bread and betrayed him.
easy.q: Who lifted up his heel against the psalmist?

answers: Because he blames only his enemies
Because he says, “I have sinned against thee”
Because his illness has nothing to do with his prayer
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks for healing while openly acknowledging his sin before God.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist’s request for healing include an acknowledgment of sin?

answers: They pray for him sincerely
They bring him medicine
They speak vanity and gather iniquity in their hearts
medium.explanation: The passage says that the visitor speaks vanity and that his heart gathers iniquity.
medium.q: What do the enemies do when they come to see the psalmist?

answers: A harmful or serious illness
A word of comfort
A word of thanksgiving
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a disease that the enemies claim has fastened upon him.
medium.q: What does “an evil disease” mean in this passage?

answers: They remain silent but act openly
They come to see him, but speak vanity and plan harm
They ask forgiveness and depart
challenge.explanation: Their visits appear outwardly concerned, but their words and thoughts are hostile.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the enemies’ visits?

answers: It moves from false visits to whispers, harmful plans, and betrayal
It moves from illness to a joyful celebration
It moves from enemies to helpful friends
challenge.explanation: The passage progresses from deceptive visits to whispering, plotting, and the betrayal of a close friend.
challenge.q: How does the description intensify the psalmist’s distress?

answers: The betrayer was an open enemy
The betrayer was a trusted companion who ate the psalmist’s bread
The betrayer had never known the psalmist
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes the companion’s closeness, trust, and shared table.
challenge.q: Why is the betrayal in the final verse especially painful?

paragraphs.idea: A Plea for Healing Amid Hostile Enemies

paragraphs.paragraph: Hope for Deliverance and Victory over Enemies
paragraphs.title: Hope for Deliverance and Victory over Enemies

answers: Hide him
Raise him up
Remove him from his country
easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to be merciful and raise him up.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

answers: Requite his enemies
Join his enemies
Forget his trouble
easy.explanation: He says, “that I may requite them.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist intend to do after being raised up?

answers: His enemy does not triumph over him
He becomes wealthy
All his enemies disappear
easy.explanation: He says, “By this I know that thou favourest me, because mine enemy doth not triumph over me.”
easy.q: What shows the psalmist that the LORD favors him?

answers: Being raised will enable him to answer his enemies
Being raised will cause him to join his enemies
There is no connection between the two
medium.explanation: He asks to be raised up so that he may requite his enemies.
medium.q: What connection does the psalmist make between being raised up and requiting his enemies?

answers: He hides his integrity
The LORD upholds him in his integrity
His integrity belongs to his enemies
medium.explanation: The psalmist says, “thou upholdest me in mine integrity.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist’s support reveal about his integrity?

answers: You have abandoned me
You have spoken against me
You have supported and strengthened me
medium.explanation: “Upholdest” means that the LORD supports and sustains him.
medium.q: What does “upholdest” mean in “thou upholdest me in mine integrity”?

answers: His enemy does not triumph over him
He is never sick from the beginning
He needs no one
challenge.explanation: The psalmist recognizes God’s favor because his enemy does not triumph over him.
challenge.q: What evidence does the psalmist give that the LORD favors him?

answers: He presents his integrity as connected with the LORD’s support
He admits that his integrity has disappeared
He says that his integrity belongs to his enemy
challenge.explanation: The psalmist connects his integrity with the LORD’s sustaining and upholding him.
challenge.q: How does “mine integrity” relate to the psalmist’s request to be raised up?

answers: The psalmist asks to disappear
The psalmist describes enduring acceptance and stability before the LORD
The psalmist asks to go over to his enemies
challenge.explanation: The expression describes being established continually before the LORD.
challenge.q: What does “settest me before thy face for ever” mean in this context?

paragraphs.idea: Hope for Deliverance and Victory over Enemies

answers: The enemies of Israel
The LORD God of Israel
The sick person
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Blessed be the LORD God of Israel.”
easy.q: Whom does the closing verse bless?

answers: From everlasting to everlasting
Until the end of the day
Only during the illness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “from everlasting, and to everlasting.”
easy.q: How long is the LORD described as existing?

answers: Blessed
Israel
Amen
easy.explanation: The verse ends with “Amen, and Amen.”
easy.q: Which word is repeated at the end?

answers: To introduce a subject about trade
To end with praise and faith in the LORD
To announce that the enemies have won
medium.explanation: The psalm concludes by blessing the LORD and affirming the words with “Amen.”
medium.q: What is the purpose of the closing blessing after the description of sickness and enemies?

answers: The blessing is directed to the LORD as the God of Israel
The blessing is directed only to one particular person
The blessing is directed toward the illness
medium.explanation: The verse identifies the LORD receiving the blessing as the God of Israel.
medium.q: What does “God of Israel” clarify about the blessing?

answers: Agreement and affirmation
Anger
Illness
medium.explanation: “Amen” expresses agreement, faith, and affirmation of the blessing.
medium.q: What does “Amen” express at the close of the psalm?

answers: The blessing is emphasized and affirmed twice
The psalmist withdraws the blessing
The psalm ends with a question
challenge.explanation: The repeated “Amen” gives the closing blessing added emphasis and affirmation.
challenge.q: What does the repetition “Amen, and Amen” suggest?

answers: It limits God’s care to the time of sickness
It presents the LORD as enduring beyond the immediate crisis
It describes the LORD as weak
challenge.explanation: The closing words widen the focus from personal trouble to the LORD’s eternal existence.
challenge.q: How does “from everlasting, and to everlasting” complete the earlier theme of deliverance?

answers: The passage moves from personal petition to a general blessing of the LORD
The passage moves from blessing to new enemies
The passage moves from illness to a journey
challenge.explanation: After the personal requests and hope for help, the psalm closes with praise to the LORD God of Israel.
challenge.q: What transition occurs between the psalmist’s requests for help and the final verse?
